newsitem.title: UK: London gold, silver close slightly firmer.
newsitem.headline: London gold, silver close slightly firmer.

text.p: Prices moved slightly higher across the precious metals complex on Wednesday afternoon, pulled ahead by trade buying in silver, dealers said.
A drawdown in silver stocks held in New York's Comex futures markets warehouses sparked the more positive sentiment.
"Everybody has been short and bearish for so long and yet the price hasn't gone down. This could be the first sign of a change today," one dealer said.
Gold closed at $381.45 per ounce up just 30 cents from Tuesday after a sleepy morning's trading.
Technical analysts said gold could expect to make progress towards $384.00 only if it could convincingly breach $381.70.
Market sentiment in gold was still mostly bearish after prices slid to 18-month lows last week within a month-old downtrend, dealers said.
"In the medium term, if there is a big price move, it's going to be lower," with $375 as the first target, one said.
The gold market would be watching for September U.S. Producer Price Index data on Friday, analysts said.

But dealers said it was unlikely to affect prices unless the figures had a significant effect on other markets. Investors have been ignoring gold in light of benign U.S. inflation and booming stock and bond market.
Silver quickly developed a nine-cent range for the day after trade buying in New York sparked the move on the basis of the warehouse drawdowns. It was last at $4.94, up four cents
Dealers have cautioned for several days that silver was looking very prone to a volatile move in either direction, but with the balance decidedly towards a fall in price.
"A nine cent range for silver is reasonably positive," one dealer said.
Silver had been even more somnolent than gold earlier opening three cents easier and struggling to hold around $4.85.
Platinum finished at $385.00 up just 50 cents. "The platinum market is thin and lacklustre," an analyst said.
The market was cautious about platinum because key Japanese demand for the metal was slack and the volume of metal stocks held by important producer Russia was a mystery, he said.
However, platinum was due for a move up after its recent drops to near 2-1/2 year lows, analysts said.
Palladium finished a dollar lower at $117.00 and was seen to be vulnerable to downside pressure after drifting below the key $120 support area again earlier this week.
